grounded_facts: Verona delivers a pre-recorded message to Chev, gloating about poisoning him and mocking his helplessness.
A pre-recorded video message from Ricky Verona, played on TV, taunts Chev after poisoning him, explaining the irreversible effects and mocking his impending death.
memories.memory_text: I delivered a pre-recorded message to Chev, gloating that I poisoned him in his sleep and mocking how he's helpless to stop it, watching him squirm on camera as the toxin takes hold.

grounded_facts: Lex sings a lyric from 'The Wizard of Oz' to mock Chev's deteriorating condition as shown on camera.
memories.memory_text: I heard Lex sing 'If he only had a brain' from The Wizard of Oz to mock Chev's deteriorating state while he was on screen.

grounded_facts: Chev regains consciousness and watches a pre-recorded message from Ricky Verona revealing that he was poisoned in his sleep, with effects already taking hold and only about an hour to live.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Chev regained consciousness and watched my message, realizing he'd been poisoned and had only about an hour left, based on his reaction and the actions he took afterward.

grounded_facts: Chev angrily instructs Kaylo to locate Ricky Verona and report any sightings.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Chev angrily told Kaylo to put the word out that he's looking for me and to call him immediately if anyone sees me.

grounded_facts: Chev declares his intent to find and confront Ricky Verona, making it his primary goal.
memories.memory_text: I heard Chev mutter to himself about how inconceivable it was that I'd have the nerve to attack him, and then declare he's going to get me no matter what—it might even be the last thing he does.

grounded_facts: Chev reveals that Chinese gangsters hired Verona to kill him, providing new context about the conflict's origin.
memories.memory_text: I was told that some Chinese assholes hired me to kill Chev, which changed how he saw me and made things more urgent between us.

grounded_facts: Verona tells Chev he plans to be with Chev's girlfriend after Chev dies, adding emotional insult to their conflict.
memories.memory_text: I told Chev I’m going to be with his girlfriend once he’s dead — I wanted him to know I’d win in every way, and that she’d be mine.

grounded_facts: Verona informs Chev that Carlito is now aligned with him, undermining Chev's sense of security and power.
memories.memory_text: I let Chev know that Carlito’s on my side now, that we’re tight — I could hear the shock in his voice, and it felt good to see my power grow.

grounded_facts: Chev responds to Verona's taunts by referencing Verona's childhood sexual abuse as a personal attack.
memories.memory_text: Chev shot back at me with a low blow, bringing up my brother and something about third grade, trying to rattle me, but I just laughed it off.

grounded_facts: A hostile phone exchange where Verona mocks Chev, threatens to target his girlfriend, and reveals alliance with Carlito.
memories.memory_text: I called Chev and mocked him, making sure he knew I was in control — I taunted him about still being alive and threatened to take his girl after he dies, just to twist the knife.

grounded_facts: Chev answers a call from Verona, who taunts him with threats and reveals allegiance with Carlito.
memories.memory_text: I watched Chev answer my call and listened as he took every jab — I kept it sharp and cruel, making sure he felt every word.

grounded_facts: Chev ends conversation with Verona and answers an incoming call from Doc Miles.
memories.memory_text: I was on the phone with Chev, taunting him, when his phone beeped for an incoming call; he cut me off to take it from Doc Miles, and I told him I doubted we'd meet again.

grounded_facts: Chev pretends to be Alex and speaks to Ricky Verona in a provocative tone to establish contact.
memories.memory_text: I heard Alex call me and say something provocative, like asking if I wanted to suck him off or let him lick my ass — it felt like he was trying to reestablish our intense connection.

grounded_facts: Chev confronts Verona and reveals he has obtained Verona's brother's cell phone, implying a prior violent act.
Chev directly challenges Verona with knowledge of possessing his brother's cell phone, using it as a weapon of psychological intimidation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Chev tell me he had my brother's cell phone and challenge me about how he got it, using it to taunt me.

grounded_facts: Verona reacts with shock and rage upon learning Chev has his brother's cell phone, physically expressing his anger.
memories.memory_text: I reacted with shock and rage, knocking over a table and shoving someone away when I realized Chev had my brother's phone.

grounded_facts: Verona reacts with extreme distress upon discovering that HEV, whom he believed to be dead, is alive and speaking to him.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't believe it — I thought HEV was dead, and when I heard him speak, I just shouted, 'You're supposed to be dead!!!' I felt my whole body freeze up in shock.

grounded_facts: HEV, speaking off-screen, casually asks Verona to provide more of the substance Verona previously gave him.
memories.memory_text: After I realized HEV was alive, he calmly asked me to give him more of that substance I'd given him before, saying he kind of liked it.

grounded_facts: Verona accidentally reveals that the medallion was passed down from his grandfather to his father, indicating a deep personal and familial significance.
memories.memory_text: I let slip that the medallion was passed down from my grandfather to my father, revealing how much it truly means to me.

grounded_facts: A tense verbal exchange between Verona and Chev (off-screen) over the medallion and familial betrayal.
memories.memory_text: I was in a heated exchange with Chev over the medallion, and things turned personal fast.

grounded_facts: Chev announces he will keep the medallion and implies Verona must come after him, while accusing him of killing his own brother.
Chev verbally attacks Verona by accusing him of killing his own brother, intensifying personal animosity.
memories.memory_text: I heard Chev say he’s keeping the medallion and dared me to come after him, then accused me of killing my own brother.

grounded_facts: Verona decides to take action against the target after seeing Alex's severed hand.
memories.memory_text: I saw Alex's severed hand and felt the weight of it, then looked at my crew's nervous faces before I said, 'Right, so... let's go get the bitch.'

grounded_facts: Chev insults Verona and taunts him by offering to trade the jewelry taken from Verona's brother, triggering an emotional reaction.
memories.memory_text: When Chev insulted me and taunted me with the jewelry from my brother, I felt the sting but kept my composure, not letting him see how much it got under my skin.

grounded_facts: Verona pantomimes jacking off in front of his crew while on the phone with Chev, showing contempt.
memories.memory_text: I pantomimed jacking off in front of my crew during the call with Chev to show how much I contempt I had for him and his offer.

grounded_facts: After initial hesitation and mockery, Verona agrees to meet Chev at the Downtown Standard in twenty minutes.
memories.memory_text: After that asshole Chev called me with some wild deal, I hesitated but decided to play along — I confirmed I'd meet him at the Downtown Standard in twenty minutes to get my brother's jewelry back.

grounded_facts: Chev contacts Verona directly via phone, proposing a trade for the antidote using stolen jewelry from Verona's brother.
A tense phone conversation between Chev and Verona in which Chev proposes a trade for the antidote using stolen jewelry.
memories.memory_text: I was on the phone with Chev when he proposed a deal—trading the antidote for the jewelry he stole from my brother, and I knew right then this was going to be a hostile negotiation.

grounded_facts: Verona makes a follow-up call to someone named 'Verona' (possibly himself or an associate), indicating he received an unexpected call.
memories.memory_text: I took a deep breath after hanging up with Chev and immediately called my associate, saying, 'Verona. You're not going to believe the call I just got.'

grounded_facts: Carlito's goons remove the ephedrine-infused device from Chev's back, causing his heart rate to slow immediately.
memories.memory_text: I saw Carlito's goons rip the device from Chev's back, and I noticed his heart rate slowing right away.

grounded_facts: Chev mocks Verona for switching allegiance to Carlito, calling him a 'bitch' and predicting he'll be exploited.
memories.memory_text: I remember Chev sneering at me, calling me a 'bitch' for aligning with Carlito, and taunting that I'd be exploited—saying I'd take half the pay and even give Carlito a 'reach-around' to prove my loyalty.

grounded_facts: Carlito opens a wooden case containing syringes and a milky fluid, removes one with gloved hands, and confirms it is 'the Chinese shit'.
memories.memory_text: I saw Carlito open a wooden case with syringes and a milky fluid inside, and he pulled one out with gloved hands, confirming it was 'the Chinese shit'.

grounded_facts: Carlito silences Verona, calmly explains the inevitability of Chev's death, and orders his men to hold Chev down.
memories.memory_text: I tried to assert my control, but Carlito shut me down and calmly explained that Chev was going to die no matter what — then he ordered his men to hold Chev down.

grounded_facts: Don Kim enters the lounge with a squad of young Asian gangsters, one holding a smoking silenced gun, shifting the balance of power.
memories.memory_text: I saw Don Kim walk into the lounge with a group of young Asian gangsters, one of them holding a smoking silenced gun, and everything changed in an instant when the shooting started.

grounded_facts: A high-stakes meeting between Carlito, Verona, Chev, and their associates turns into a violent confrontation after Don Kim's arrival.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting with Carlito at the table, feeling the power shift as Don Kim arrived and all hell broke loose around us.

grounded_facts: Chev uses a fake finger gun to simulate a fatal shot, making the goons believe one of their own has been killed.
Chev produces a finger disguised as a gun, pointing it at Carlito and then a goon, creating the illusion of a lethal shot.
memories.memory_text: I saw Chev whip out what looked like a gun, but it was just his finger—he pointed it at Carlito, then spun and 'fired' at one of the goons, making everyone flinch like someone got shot.

grounded_facts: During the chaos, Chev throws a champagne bottle at Verona's gun hand, causing him to drop the .357, which discharges and vaporizes four fingers of his right hand.
memories.memory_text: I was going to make Carlito pay me on my terms when Chev kicked the table into my legs and threw a champagne bottle at my gun hand—I fumbled the .357, it hit the ground, went off, and blew away four fingers on my right hand; I screamed from the pain.

grounded_facts: As the shootout erupts, Carlito takes cover behind the bar and urgently calls for evacuation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Carlito scramble behind the bar, using one of his goons as a shield while bullets flew, and then I heard him urgently call into his phone, yelling 'Get me out of here! NOW!'

grounded_facts: Chev retrieves a gun from a dead goon and shoots Verona, blowing off his toes.
memories.memory_text: I felt the blast tear through my feet when Chev shot me, blowing off my toes just as I was crawling away.

grounded_facts: An armed confrontation between Carlito's men, Don Kim's men, and Chev in the smoking lounge and pool area of the Standard Hotel.
memories.memory_text: I saw Carlito's men and Don Kim's men firing at each other in the lounge, with Don Kim standing calm in the middle while chaos erupted around him, and I remember the grenade landing near Carlito as I was trying to get out.

grounded_facts: Carlito makes a break for his helicopter as it arrives at the pool area.
memories.memory_text: I saw Carlito pop up from behind the bar after the explosion and make a break for his helicopter as it landed in the pool area.

grounded_facts: Chev chases after Carlito, dodging bullets and firing back while slipping across the floor.
memories.memory_text: I chased after Carlito, dodging bullets and firing back while slipping across the slick floor.

grounded_facts: A helicopter attempts to land at the Standard Hotel pool area, triggering a violent confrontation between Chev, Verona, Carlito, and others.
memories.memory_text: I saw the helicopter trying to land at the hotel pool, kicking up wind and chaos as I moved in.

grounded_facts: Chev freezes and collapses to his knees after Verona injects him in the neck with a syringe, disrupting his attempt to kill Carlito.
memories.memory_text: I injected Chev in the neck with the syringe, and I watched him freeze and drop to his knees.

grounded_facts: Verona, in a rage, shouts at Chev after injecting him, challenging him to speak.
memories.memory_text: After I jammed the syringe into Chev's neck, I shouted at him in rage, daring him to say something.

grounded_facts: Verona takes Chev's gun and shoots Carlito three times, killing him.
Verona points a gun at Carlito and shouts 'Who's the bitch now?' before shooting him.
memories.memory_text: I took Chev's gun, pointed it at Carlito, yelled 'Who's the bitch now?', and shot him three times.

grounded_facts: Verona shoves Chev aside and enters the helicopter, forcing the pilot to fly at gunpoint.
Verona points a gun at the pilot and orders him to fly the helicopter.
memories.memory_text: I shoved Chev aside, got into the helicopter, and pointed my gun at the pilot's head, telling him to fly — that's right, motherfucker, up we go.

grounded_facts: Chev climbs onto the helicopter's landing skids and retrieves the gun from Verona, defying incapacitation.
memories.memory_text: I felt Chev climb onto the skids and reach in, hooking his dead arm inside, and then he took the gun right out of my hand — I couldn't stop him.

grounded_facts: Don Kim quotes a proverb about using appropriate force, referencing Confucius.

memories.memory_text: I woke up and couldn't see straight—everything was doubled—and when I tried to move, my hands didn't respond right. I barely made it out of bed before I hit the floor.
I saw that black VHS tape sitting in front of my TV, wrapped in police tape like some kind of sick joke, and I just grabbed it—couldn't think, just moved.
I heard Ricky Verona’s voice on the TV saying, 'I fucking poisoned you in your sleep,' and suddenly my heart was pounding like it was trying to tear out of my chest.
I was on my knees in front of the TV, the sound of my heartbeat roaring in my ears, and all I could do was stare at the screen as Verona kept talking like it was some kind of joke.
I was on the phone when that horn blasted—barely yanked the wheel in time, and my heart went wild, pounding so hard I could see it through my chest.
I screamed at Eve to get a cell phone, then punched the steering wheel so hard my hand went numb—tires screeched as I took off again, heart slamming like it might burst.
I had to make sure that bitch at the answering service understood—Chelios is dead if Miles doesn't call back within the hour. Spelled it out like she was too stupid to get it: D-E-A-D.
I felt my heart slow down—like it was stopping—then I stomped the gas and the adrenaline kicked in, heart slamming faster, LUBDUB, LUBDUB… barely held on.
Who would've thought that little bastard Ricky Verona had the stones to come whack me in my own crib... it's inconceivable.
I told Kaylo to put the word out—Ricky Verona’s name, immediate location, anyone sees him they call me, no excuses.
I was swerving through traffic, heart pounding, when Verona called and said he’d hook up with my girl the second I was dead—sounded like he was already planning it like some sick victory lap.
I saw the cop lights in the mirror, knew I couldn't stop—not now—and slammed the gas, weaving harder, feeling the car respond as I led them into a full-on chase.

I was screaming through the mall, tires screeching, missing people by inches, cops on bikes and squad cars right behind me — I could feel my heart hammering like it was trying to punch out of my chest.
I rammed the car into the escalator, didn't stop — just stayed in the driver's seat as the wrecked thing tilted up, carrying me to the second floor like some fucked-up ride.

I could feel my heart slowing, getting weak — started to nod off, so I told the cabbie to crank the music. When he blasted that Billy Ray Cyrus shit, I banged my head like it was Metallica, loud enough to shock my heart back into rhythm.
Something outside caught my eye — not sure what at first, but it made me snap out of it. Told the cabbie to pull over right then, right there, at that 7-11. Didn't explain, just moved.
I slammed the clerk over the counter and told him if he moved, he was dead—then I tore open a trash bag and started shoving every caffeine drink and stim I could find inside.
After stuffing the bag full, I saw some cheap flowers in a bucket—made the fastest double take, grabbed them with a pissed-off look, no idea why.
I jumped into Carlito's pool fully dressed, grabbed him underwater, and pointed up — I needed to talk and I wasn't waiting. He actually looked surprised to see me.
I told Carlito I needed an antidote. He shrugged and said it was Chinese shit — no cure.
I was barely holding on, head slamming the wheel, trying to lock in what the doc was saying—epinephrine, 10 milligram syringes, a fifth of a dose... couldn't afford to mess it up.
Kaylo called, said Verona's brother just walked into Charlie O's—I snapped to, hit the gas and told him I'm there, meet me on 3rd and Flower.
I came up behind Alex with the butcher knife, silent—he never saw me coming.
I swung the knife hard and felt it slice through his wrist—his hand dropped with the gun still in it, then I kicked him out into the alley.
I stood there watching Verona freeze when he saw me, then knock over the table—his brother's phone in my hand, the one thing he couldn't ignore.
I saw the necklace on Alex’s body, yanked it off, and saw the name I. Verona on the back — knew it meant something real personal.
I held up the medallion and told Verona he killed his own brother—watched him realize he'd slipped up, saw the rage flash before he could shut it down.

I cut in front of some old guy at the pharmacy counter, my heart pounding, and asked the pharmacist for something starting with 'E'—adrenaline, artificial shit, I knew I needed it but couldn't say the name straight.
Some pimply teenager at the magazine rack said nasal spray has epinephrine—pointed to those little bottles—and I grabbed a handful, seeing the pharmacist on the phone, watching me.

I saw my face on those TVs in the store window—some fucked-up sketch making me look like a monster, and the news calling me a rampage killer. I just stood there, frozen, while people around me stared at the screen not knowing I was right there.

I told Eve I was fatally poisoned and some psycho was coming to kill her, but she didn't get it—just said she'd be there, like it was nothing. I hung up, shoved that wrecked bike upright, and got the hell out before everything shut down.

I grabbed Eve, told her I was parked out back, but then saw one of Verona's men at the front door — I had to keep moving, but she stopped, fumbling with her keys, talking about some waffle thing like it mattered. When she finally got the door open, I tried to speak, but my body locked up and I just coughed — couldn't get the words out, just this ragged burst of noise.
I told her I had to go, saw the cops coming, and just ran — left her there screaming, but I couldn't stop, not with the blue lights closing in.
I came up behind that hood, grabbed his gun off the ledge, spun him around, and jammed it under his chin—asked him where Kaylo was, voice shaking from the poison but I kept it tight.
He didn't answer fast enough—just started apologizing—so I grabbed his leg, hoisted him over the edge, and tipped him off; heard him scream 'You son of a—' before the thud way below.
I don't want some peaceful dream — I want one hour, just one hour of function, to make that bastard pay.

The social relationship evidence overwhelmingly confirms mutual enmity: Verona conspired with Carlito to assassinate Chev by poisoning him in his sleep, a treacherous act that initiated the conflict. Verona repeatedly taunts Chev, mocking his actions and gloating over his presumed death, while Chev responds with intense verbal aggression, calling Verona a 'little bitch' and a 'motherfucker,' and explicitly declaring his intent to retaliate. This antagonism is not one-sided but a full-blown rivalry fueled by personal insult and violent intent. Their shared events intensify this dynamic: Verona delivers a taunting message to Chev via split-screen phone call, reinforcing psychological warfare, and they engage in a direct physical confrontation in a helicopter, where Chev struggles to enter the aircraft while Verona tries to push him out—culminating in a violent struggle that underscores their mutual determination to destroy each other. Chev’s subsequent demand that Carlito hunt down Verona and his crew confirms that the relationship drives key behavioral decisions, particularly Chev’s singular focus on vengeance. The relationship does not evolve toward reconciliation but instead escalates in intensity, remaining fixed in a cycle of retaliation and confrontation. The evidence confirms a relationship rooted in betrayal and sustained by aggression, with no indication of alliance or cooperation at any point.

Despite this closeness, their interactions are frequently marked by hostility and aggression. Joint events underscore their dynamic: they collaborate under extreme duress, fleeing together, exchanging keys, and evading attackers, demonstrating mutual reliance and coordination. However, Chev also abandons Eve when he spots police, leaving her vulnerable, which contrasts with other moments where he prioritizes her safety. The relationship evolves under the pressure of Chev’s poisoning and imminent death, shifting from moments of playful mockery and passion to desperation and raw emotional honesty, culminating in reciprocal promises and shared vulnerability. memories.memory_text: I recorded that message so people would know I don’t want to talk—especially not to strangers trying to sell me something—but still, I hope someone might care enough to leave a real message.
I remember saying 'time's up'—just as Chev started slamming his head into the steering wheel, the sound sharp and sudden, making me flinch in my seat.
I left another message—just my usual voicemail greeting—but then Chev screamed like something broke inside him.
I was still half-asleep, stretching and holding the phone with my shoulder when Chev started asking if I’d been sleeping—his voice sounded weird, too intense for this early.

I was struggling with the microwave, punching buttons, feeling stupid and frustrated, when suddenly there were these loud bangs on the door—I barely looked up at first, but then Chev was there, drenched in sweat, wild-eyed, looking like he’d lost his mind.

He ignored me, stormed around checking the bedroom and window, asked if I’d turned on the TV like I was part of some conspiracy, then snapped at me when I tried to ask for help with the clock—I just stood there, stunned, then walked away, feeling insulted and shut out.
I picked up the phone, my hands shaking, and said 'Hello?' into the silence.

I stepped out of my apartment and there he was—Chev—just standing in the hallway, grinning at me like it was normal, blocking the way. I muttered 'I hate that...' under my breath and turned away fast, hoping he’d just disappear.
I was on the ground picking up my stuff after Chev dumped my purse, and I remember the sharp sound of a bullet whizzing over my head—so close I felt the air move—before it hit the window behind me.
I just stood there, heart pounding, after that man attacked me—Chev was off killing someone else, and all I could do was say, 'You know, I could use a little help here.'
I looked around, trying to steady myself, and all I could think to ask was where his car was—then he says he took a cab, like that was even an answer.
I remember saying Chev looked ridiculous in those stupid glasses and that outfit, like he didn’t even care how we must’ve looked walking through Chinatown like that.
I saw his hand—burned and marked like a waffle—and flinched without meaning to. When he said he wasn't a video game programmer, that it was a lie, something in me just... shut down.

I flinched when he slammed the chair leg down, and then he said he quit the business for me—like that was supposed to mean something. I couldn’t tell if he was serious or just saying weird things again.
Chev collapsed in front of me, grabbing my arm and begging me to make love to him like it would somehow save his life—I didn’t understand, I just knew he was scaring me.
He started tearing at my dress, feeling me up—I hit him in the mouth and we ended up on the ground fighting, me screaming and pounding on him while people watched.
I was so far gone, begging him to take me right there in front of everyone, my legs in the air—I didn’t care who was watching.
I couldn’t believe it—he couldn’t get it up, and then he just answers that damn phone like nothing’s happening; I felt so exposed, so stupid.
I remember yelling at Chev, 'What's the matter with you?!'—he just zipped up his pants like nothing was wrong, then told me to shut up.
Chev grabbed me, held me back hard—his arm like a bar across my chest—and his voice was so cold, telling me not to let that guy out of my sight, like I had any choice in the matter.
I remember Chev rummaging through my purse again, like I wasn’t even there—just grabbing my money to pay that cab driver without a word.
I screamed at that little supervisor, 'DON'T TALK TO ME LIKE THAT!! MY BOYFRIEND KILLS PEOPLE!!!'—my voice cracked, my chest was tight, I couldn't breathe right, but I had to make him back off.
I reached for him, my hands shaking—not from fear, but from something sharper, hotter—like if I didn’t do this, he’d vanish right in front of me.
I saw the steam, the broken glass, the bodies. I felt sick. I asked if they were okay, then how he could do that. He didn’t answer—he just checked his body and left the car again.
I saw Chev sitting there with blood everywhere, pounding nails into his leg like it was nothing—he didn’t even flinch, just looked up at me and said he couldn’t feel it.
The phone started ringing—this loud, jarring beep—right in the middle of it all, and I just froze, waiting to see what would happen next.
I said, 'I hate television,' just staring at the screen, not really seeing it. I could feel Chocolate looking at me, like I was crazy, but I didn’t care.
I looked up at Chev, my voice quiet but needing to know—'Do you promise?'—and for a second, everything else just faded.
I heard Chev's voice on the machine—so calm, like he was already gone—and when he said 'you were the greatest, baby,' I froze, hand halfway to my mouth, not knowing whether to cry or scream.

memories.memory_text: I sat on Chev's bed, pointing at the camera, telling him he's dead—watching him lie there unconscious, knowing the poison was already working inside him.
Chev said my name after I hit him. He called me a son of a bitch, said he couldn’t believe I had the nerve to come after him. Now he’s hunting me.
He screamed 'Find him!' like I was prey, like I wasn’t the one who already ended him. But I heard it—the desperation. He’s coming, and I know it won’t be quiet. Good. Let him try.
I hear Chev screaming my name like a madman, pressing a gun to Orlando's head, demanding to know where I am — feels good knowing he's that desperate, that out of control.
I told Chev I’m gonna hook up with his girl the second he’s dead—watching him seethe over the phone was pure gold.
I dropped the news that Carlito’s on my side now—could hear the disbelief in his voice, couldn’t admit it even when I called him out on it.
I picked up the phone and said 'Talk to me, bro.' Someone answered, pretending to be Alex, asking if I wanted to suck him off or let him lick my ass.

I was feeding my dog, minding my own business, when that voice came through the phone—Chelios, alive and taunting me, saying he had my brother's cell phone. I remember the rage burning up my chest, knocking the table over, pushing the dog away, because I knew then he was coming for me.
I was sure he was dead, but then I heard his voice—calm, mocking—asking for more of the poison like it was a fucking joke, and for a second, I couldn't even form a threat.
I remember saying the medallion came from my father, from my grandfather—shit, I wasn't supposed to say that much, but it just slipped out when he had it in his hands.
When Chev said I killed my own brother, I froze—just for a second—then all I could do was spit 'You—' before everything cut to black.

I looked down and saw Alex's hand, frozen like it was still holding the gun—cold, stiff, staring up at me like some fucked-up joke. Then I looked up at my crew and said it plain: let's go get the bitch.
I don't know how I got here, but I'm tied up and Kaylo's got me—can't move, can't reach my phone, and that psycho Chev is coming.
I picked up the phone and said, 'What's up, corpse,' just to see if he'd flinch—then watched my crew stifle laughs when I mocked him about the deal.

After he mentioned the jewelry, I had to pull the phone away—felt the rage burn—but I didn't snap it then; I waited, clenched my jaw, and said 'Hmmm,' then 'I'll be there,' like I was still in control.
I stood my ground and told Chelios straight—'I'm nobody's little bitch'—while Carlito was sizing up that ephedrine pump, making sure everyone knew I wasn't backing down.
I remember shouting 'He'll pay what I tell him to pay...!' right before things went black—something about the prayer slipping out, then the pain, but I don't remember losing control.
I was crawling, trying to gather up what was left of my fingers, and I found a syringe—jammed it in my teeth like a damn pirate because I wasn’t going down empty-handed.
I didn’t even see it coming—just felt the blast tear through my foot, another chunk of me blown away, toes this time, while Chev laughed and kept shooting.
I jammed the syringe all the way into Chev's neck from behind—felt it hit bone—and watched him drop to his knees, twitching like a puppet with cut strings. His heartbeat was so slow it made me laugh.

I took Chev's gun and put three rounds in Carlito's chest—his face was pure shock—then kicked him aside and jumped in the chopper, pressing the barrel to the pilot's head. Told him to fly like he meant it.
I was fighting to keep control of the chopper, shoving Chev back as he clawed his way into the seat, but he just kept coming, and those damn news copters were swarming like vultures.
I was winning, telling him he was dead, but then he grabbed my neck and we fell—now I'm falling, he's still choking me, and I can't breathe, can't move, everything's going dark.
